recipes.title: Spicy Italian Sausage and Pepperoni Flatbread Pizza
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the sausage meat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, and cook until browned and cooked through (5-7 minutes). Drain excess fat.
Brush both sides of the naan flatbreads lightly with the remaining olive oil and place them on the baking sheet.
Spread pizza sauce evenly over each flatbread, leaving a thin border around the edges.
Evenly distribute shredded mozzarella, cooked Italian sausage, and chopped pepperoni across the flatbreads.
Bake in the preheated oven for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are golden crisp and cheese is bubbly and melted.
Garnish with chopped fresh basil, slice into wedges, and serve.
recipes.swaps: Mild Italian sausage can be substituted for hot sausage; pita bread can be used in place of naan.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Skillet, baking sheet, chef's knife or pizza cutter. Fast, flavorful dinner with balanced browning.

recipes.title: Creamy Tuscan Sausage Pasta

ingredients.name: dry white wine (or chicken broth with 1 tsp lemon juice)

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for the pasta.
Heat a 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add bulk Italian sausage, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, and brown until cooked through (5-6 minutes). Remove sausage from skillet and set aside.
Add olive oil to the pan drippings if needed. Add diced onion and minced garlic; sauté over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until golden brown.
Stir in Italian seasoning, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, white wine, and Dijon mustard. Simmer briskly until the liquid reduces almost completely.
Add pasta to boiling water and cook until al dente according to package directions, draining when ready.
Pour heavy cream into the skillet with the sun-dried tomato mixture. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until lightly thickened.
Add chopped baby spinach to the skillet and stir just until wilted.
Return the cooked sausage to the pan, then fold in the drained hot pasta, simmering together for 1-2 minutes so the sauce clings to noodles.
Stir in grated parmesan cheese, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve immediately.
recipes.swaps: Spicy Italian sausage can replace mild sausage; coconut cream can replace heavy cream for dairy-free.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Large pasta pot, 10-inch skillet, wooden spoon. Watch cream closely as it simmers to prevent boil-over.
